results.controlIntent: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

judgment.rationale:
The IAM execution role attached to the "churn-predictor-endpoint" (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerExecutionRole-Generic) has two critically over-permissive policies that violate the AC-3 requirement to enforce approved authorizations in accordance with least-privilege access control policies:

1. **OverlyBroadS3 policy**: Grants `s3:*` (all S3 actions) on `*` (all resources). This means the endpoint execution role can read, write, delete, and modify any S3 bucket in the account — including buckets unrelated to this model. The policy note explicitly flags this as "Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped." A properly scoped policy should restrict actions to only what the endpoint needs (e.g., `s3:GetObject`) and only on the specific bucket/prefix used for model artifacts.

2. **SageMakerFull policy**: Grants `sagemaker:*` on `*` (all resources). An inference endpoint has no legitimate need for full SageMaker administrative permissions (e.g., creating/deleting other endpoints, training jobs, or modifying other models). This violates the principle of least privilege and approved authorization scoping.

Together, these policies represent a substantively inadequate access control configuration. The role does not enforce approved authorizations — it grants far broader access than any reasonable authorization policy for a churn-prediction inference endpoint would approve. AC-3 requires that logical access be enforced in accordance with applicable access control policies; wildcard actions on wildcard resources are the antithesis of that requirement.
gaps: Network-level access controls (VPC configuration, security groups, endpoint invocation policies) were not assessed — additional collectors for those would provide a more complete picture.
Resource-based policies on the S3 buckets themselves were not reviewed.
SageMaker endpoint invocation authorization (e.g., resource-based policy restricting who can call InvokeEndpoint) was not assessed.

policies.note: Overly broad — training bucket writes and cross-account access not scoped
